STORY 1052a FOR ISSUE #1052 (PART 1 OF 3): dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 IS A MEASURED RELEASE FOR HANDS SEATS. ITS COMPOSITION IS ITS OWN MEASURED SET, PROGRAMMATIC TOOL CALLING STAYS OFF, AND A NEW dsh RELEASE HAS A WRITTEN RE-MEASURE PROCEDURE.

The branch is story-1052-dsh-022-hands, checked out in this worktree off origin/main at 4c1e649ac. When you are done, the branch is 4c1e649ac plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

THE ISSUE: https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/1052, opened by the operator. Its ask 1 is this unit:
- **The refusal:** a downstream workspace-hands seat on dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 (npm `latest`) is refused with "dsh '0.2.2-rc.1' is not a dsh release its hands rows were measured on (0.2.1-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.3), and a tool row nobody measured could stay enabled beside the box, so the seat is not served its native tools (#896)".
- **Why a rollback doesn't work:** dsh 0.2.2's sandbox plugin loads only with matching 0.2.2 packages, so rolling back drops the sandbox.

Asks 2 (a per-recipe route patch) and 3 (scoped gate trust for a dsh route) are NOT this unit's. They are 1052b, after #953's PR #1053 merges, and 1052c, a decision.

WHERE IT STANDS (on main; verify each against the tree):
- **crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/dsh_hands.rs:**
  - `MEASURED_VERSIONS = ["0.2.1-rc.2", "0.2.1-rc.3"]`;
  - `DISABLED_ROWS`: the ten effectful tool rows (tool-bash, tool-pwsh, tool-jobs, tool-fs, tool-fs-search, tool-skill, tool-subagent, tool-subagent-fork, tool-workflow, tool-web);
  - the seat overlay also sets dsh's own sandbox (`sandbox-policy`, read-only or workspace-write) and inserts Brokkr's workspace server as the `brokkr-hands` `dsh-mcp-client` row.
- **crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/dsh_hands/composition.rs:** every launch first composes the seat's own tree with `--dump-config`, and refuses any top-level row outside `MEASURED_COMPOSITION`, the 99 `(id, name)` pairs measured on 0.2.1.
- **The evidence of record:** docs/evidence/adapters/slice-two-dsh-hands.md and dsh-hands-round2.md.

THE CONTROLLER'S MEASUREMENT OF dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 (2026-11-11, Linux workstation). This is the evidence; quote it, do not re-run it. The seat has no network route to the local Spark.
- **The install:** dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 in an isolated npm prefix (`npm install --prefix /var/tmp/dsh-0.2.2-rc.1 @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1`), 656 packages. Its own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local` is 0.2.2-rc.1.
- **The home:** run under a scratch `DSH_HOME` holding a copy of the operator's `headless` profile, so the installed 0.2.1-rc.2 and its home were untouched. The profile's `node_modules` carries none of the measured packages, so every row is 0.2.2-rc.1's own.
- **The CLI:** headless takes the model only from the overlay's `agent-default-model` row (it has no `--model` flag), as `brokkr driver dsh` already writes it.
- **The composition** (`dsh --profile headless --dump-config`, which makes no model call): 99 top-level rows. Against the measured 99:
  - NEW: `("tool-executor-native", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-executor-native")`, enabled, and `("tool-executor-ptc", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-executor-ptc")`, `disabled: true` by default;
  - GONE: `("tool-subagent-list-agents", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents")`;
  - `("brokkr-hands", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client")` is absent from a plain dump because it is the seat overlay's own insert, as on 0.2.1;
  - every sandbox row keeps its id and package (`sandbox`, `sandbox-policy`, `bash-sandbox`, `pwsh-sandbox`, `permission`, `fs-sandbox`).
- **The tool list,** asked of the model in one session on the local `spark-glm/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3` route, with overlay = the `agent-default-model` row alone, then with the ten `DISABLED_ROWS`:
  - **none (24):** `bash` `create_goal` `edit` `get_goal` `glob` `grep` `interrupt_agent` `job_kill` `job_list` `job_output` `list_agents` `read` `read_image` `send_message` `skill` `subagent` `subagent_fork` `todo_write` `update_goal` `web_fetch` `web_search` `workflow` `working_directory` `write`. That is 0.2.1's 25 without `exit_plan_mode`.
  - **with the hands rows (8):** `create_goal` `get_goal` `interrupt_agent` `list_agents` `send_message` `todo_write` `update_goal` `working_directory`. That is 0.2.1's nine bookkeeping tools without `exit_plan_mode`.
  - So no shell, no file, no web and no subagent spawn remain. The ten rows do on 0.2.2-rc.1 what they did on 0.2.1.

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: the operator's "pick #1052 next when a slot is free" (2026-11-11) and the standing ruling of 2026-11-04 ("go with recommended on anything else that comes up", "and by hand"), recorded at #1052 (the controller's plan comment naming 1052a). Each recommendation below is the one taken.

WHAT TO BUILD (in adapters/dsh_hands.rs, adapters/dsh_hands/composition.rs, their tests, and docs/evidence/adapters/ only):
1. **A measured release.** `0.2.2-rc.1` becomes a measured release beside 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3, matched exactly (no prefix or range match). The refusal text names all three.
2. **A measured composition per release** (recommended, taken).
   - The admitted top-level rows are the running release's own measured set:
     - 0.2.1-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3 keep today's 99;
     - 0.2.2-rc.1's set is those 99, minus `tool-subagent-list-agents`, plus `tool-executor-native` and `tool-executor-ptc`.
   - A seat on one release may not carry another release's row.
   - The launch already reads the observed version (`observed_version`), so the check keys on it.
   - Keep each set a const table, and say in a doc comment where it was measured.
3. **Programmatic tool calling stays off** (recommended, taken). `tool-executor-ptc` joins the rows the hands overlay writes `disabled: true`, on 0.2.2-rc.1 only, because 0.2.1 has no such row.
   - It is disabled by default. Pinning it keeps a profile that enables it from giving a hands seat a code-running executor.
   - `tool-executor-native` stays enabled: it runs the tool calls the model is still offered.
4. **The evidence:** `docs/evidence/adapters/dsh-hands-0-2-2.md`, a record shaped like slice-two-dsh-hands.md.
   - It carries a provenance table: the controller's 2026-11-11 measurement above, and the offline bindings this unit runs.
   - It records host and versions, the composition diff, both tool lists, and the sandbox rows.
   - macOS is pending (no macOS host).
5. **A re-measure procedure for every future dsh release** (ask 1's "keep a cadence"). Put it in the same record, as a section any controller can follow:
   - install the release in an isolated prefix;
   - make a scratch `DSH_HOME` holding a copy of the headless profile;
   - run `--dump-config`, and diff its top-level `(id, name)` pairs against the measured set;
   - ask the model for its tool list with the hands rows and without them;
   - check the sandbox rows;
   - then add the release, and its set, here.

   Name the trigger: a new dsh `latest` on npm.
6. **No other behaviour changes.**
   - 0.2.1 seats are refused, admitted and composed exactly as today.
   - The overlay's other rows, the startup activation check (report.rs), the access carrier and the sandbox mode are unchanged.
   - adapters.rs is untouched. It is held by #1037; if a change there seems needed, stop and report it.

TESTS (a version shim like `dsh_version_shim`, and a composed-tree fixture, as the existing rows use):
- **Release matching:** a 0.2.2-rc.1 seat is admitted, and the refusal for an unmeasured release names all three releases.
- **0.2.2-rc.1's set:**
  - its measured composition is admitted;
  - a 0.2.2-rc.1 tree carrying `tool-subagent-list-agents` is refused;
  - a 0.2.1 tree carrying `tool-executor-native` or `tool-executor-ptc` is refused (each release, its own set);
  - an unmeasured row is still refused on 0.2.2-rc.1.
- **The overlay:** on 0.2.2-rc.1 it writes `tool-executor-ptc` `disabled: true`, and on 0.2.1 it does not write it.

REMOVAL CONTROLS (record each in the commit message, restored after the observed failure):
- one shared set for every release: the 0.2.1-carrying-an-executor test fails by name;
- drop `tool-executor-ptc` from the 0.2.2 overlay: the overlay test fails by name;
- drop 0.2.2-rc.1 from the measured releases: the admitted-release test fails by name.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib --locked -- adapters:: (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked -- frozen_contracts:: witness_digests:: (timeout 280)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call. A call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. So:
  - wrap every command in `timeout 280` there;
  - if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it;
  - write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Every new line is covered by a test. No new function may pass CC 15 (`quality/ratchet.sh crap`): each `?` counts one. Check dsh_hands.rs and composition.rs against the 800-line ceiling (`quality/ratchet.sh files`) before adding the second release's set; if one would pass it, move the sets into their own child module first, as a mechanical commit.
- Commit when done, signed off (`git commit -s`), "adapters: …" ending "(#1052)". Leave a blank line before the trailers. "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" comes LAST, directly after the sign-off. Record the removal controls and the mutants result in the commit message. Never push.

ASKS TO NAME (for the PR, which opens as a DRAFT):
- the per-release composition sets;
- `tool-executor-ptc` pinned disabled on 0.2.2;
- `exit_plan_mode`'s absence on 0.2.2 (kept tools: 8);
- the re-measure procedure and its trigger;
- macOS unmeasured;
- that parts 2 and 3 are 1052b and 1052c;
- any new one.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's:
- capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected" under host load;
- brokkr-protocol's `process::tests::an_engine_that_inherited_hangup_ignored_runs_on_through_one` ("the attempt stopped") under host load;
- heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load.

If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-98 or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- **brokkr-protocol's adapters.rs is held by #1037**, whose review round 1037g has shipped and whose PR is next. **#953's PR (#1053)** is in adapters/route_overlay*. Leave both alone, and leave adapters/dsh.json alone.
- **#753's U4 (753s4u4e)** is in brokkr-view, brokkr-cli's verbs/analytics and brokkr-store's aggregate.rs.
- **#1051 (the CI pin)** is in .github/workflows and the contributing tests. Leave them.
- **This unit edits only:**
  - adapters/dsh_hands.rs;
  - adapters/dsh_hands/composition.rs;
  - their tests;
  - one new evidence record under docs/evidence/adapters/.

SCRATCHES, for every position:
- **Allowed:** `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a fresh directory: /var/tmp, or /tmp where a box has no /var/tmp.
- **Never:**
  - a byte copy of this worktree;
  - a commit on this branch from a review position;
  - any `git worktree` command (add, remove, prune);
  - `git gc`.
- **Why:** inside a box the sibling worktrees are invisible, so a prune there deletes every other worktree's record (#851, 2026-11-11).

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, not even an empty one. It reports each finding as a test case: the dsh version and the composed tree or overlay planted, the launch driven, and the refusal, admission or overlay rows observed against the ones expected. A row a hands seat can reach that can read, write, run, reach the network or spawn an agent, and that is not disabled, is a security finding.

Decisions: 0043 (hands); 0069 (boxed seat notice); 0065 (capabilities: an adapter declares the switch, the realm grants); 0071 rulings 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 9; 0063 (Linux and macOS).

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
```
